eligibility: Holders of an LCL bank card on an LCL current account (personal customers). The clause sits in the card's Dispositions Générales; it is in the 2026 Visa Cléo terms and in the (older) Visa Premier, Visa Infinite and Inventive Mastercard/MacarteLCL terms. Both immediate-debit and deferred-debit cards qualify, because the terms set a timing for each. Whether it is available on Mouv by LCL, the virtual card, the Visa Crédit Renouvelable or L by LCL wasn't established.
optIn: Opt-in, free. The customer can activate it when subscribing to the card, at any time in the LCL Mes Comptes app (takes effect the next business day, 'avec effet le jour ouvré suivant'), online in the Espace Client, or in a branch. Naming a child's account as beneficiary means contacting the branch with the child's account number. Switching between 1 € and 5 €, changing the beneficiary and deactivating are free and possible at any time.
eligiblePurchases: Every card payment made in euros ('pour chaque paiement effectué en euros'; the page says 'chaque achat réglé en euros avec votre carte bancaire LCL'). Neither the terms nor the page treat in-store, online and contactless payments differently, and none is excluded.
excluded: Cash withdrawals ('Les retraits espèces ne sont pas concernés'). Payments in other currencies, by implication of 'en euros'. Direct debits, transfers and cheques aren't card payments and aren't covered. Mobile-wallet payments (Apple Pay and others) aren't mentioned.
method: Unit choice: the customer chooses whether each euro payment is rounded up to the next 1 € or the next 5 €, and the difference is saved (22.55 € moves 0.45 € or 2.45 €). Neither the page nor the terms state a default unit. There is no fixed amount, no multiplier and no cap.
sourceAccount: The current account the card operates on ('Le versement du total des arrondis est débité du compte sur lequel fonctionne la Carte').
destination: Up to two beneficiary accounts, credited with the whole amount or half each: a Livret A, a Livret de Développement Durable et Solidaire, a Livret Jeune, or any non-regulated savings account (CSL etc.) held at LCL in the cardholder's name or in the name of a child they legally represent. The customer can also give all or part of the round-ups to an association LCL has selected (the page names Mécénat Chirurgie Cardiaque, with a tax receipt each January). The LEP and the PEL/CEL aren't listed.
timing: The round-ups accumulate and their total is transferred in one sweep: each 'quinzaine' (half-month, every two weeks) for immediate-debit cards, and at each month end for deferred-debit cards. The marketing page says 'vous serez débité en plus de la différence' at each purchase, but the terms make it one transfer a period.
insufficientFunds: Never overdraws. If a period's transfer would leave the card's account in debit, or would take a regulated beneficiary account (Livret A, LDDS, Livret Jeune) over its legal ceiling, that period's transfer is cancelled in full: 'il sera alors annulé en totalité pour la période concernée'. It isn't made partially and isn't carried into the next period, because the whole period is dropped.
refunds: Not addressed. Neither the terms nor the page say whether a round-up is reversed when a purchase is refunded or cancelled.
closure: The option is deactivated automatically, with immediate effect, when the beneficiary account closes (unless another is named before the transfer date), when the card's account closes, when the card is lost, stolen or used fraudulently, when it is withdrawn, or when the card contract ends. If two beneficiaries are named, closing either one deactivates the option. On deactivation, round-ups accumulated before it are not credited ('ne seront pas crédités'), so a pending half-month or month of round-ups is lost. This rule appears in the terms from 07/12/2023 on. The 2020 Inventive terms said the opposite ('seront crédités'). The option carries over to a renewed or replacement card.
unknowns: What happens to a payment that is already a whole euro (or a multiple of 5 €): does it move nothing, or a full unit?
Whether a refunded or cancelled purchase reverses its round-up.
Whether the 'not credited on deactivation' rule also covers automatic deactivation (account closure, card loss). The sentence sits under customer deactivation, and the terms don't say otherwise.
The exact day of the fortnightly and month-end sweeps, and whether a cancelled period's round-ups are simply discarded (the terms say only 'annulé en totalité pour la période concernée').

Which current LCL cards carry the option: the 2026 Cléo terms do, and older Premier, Infinite and Inventive terms do; Mouv by LCL, the virtual card, the revolving-credit card and L by LCL were not established.
Whether mobile-wallet (Apple Pay, Google Pay) and foreign online payments in euros count. The terms say only 'chaque paiement effectué en euros'.
Whether there is a monthly cap on round-ups. None is stated.
slateRecord: SLATE (ACCOUNT_LIFE['fr-lcl'].roundUp, 2026-09-26): "System'Épargne: free option; every card purchase is rounded up to the next euro and the difference is swept to an LCL savings account (own or a child's): end of month for deferred-debit cards, every two weeks for immediate-debit cards; cancelable free from the next day." fr-lcl is not in ROUND_UP_AMOUNT, so SLATE moves the change to the next whole euro. (1) The record is incomplete on the unit. The bank's current terms and page let the customer choose 1 € or 5 €, and SLATE models only 1 €. That is one of the two choices, so the euro default is a defensible estimate, but the words should name both units. Under ROUND_UP_AMOUNT's own definition (a customer choice with no stated default), fr-lcl arguably belongs there as { chosen: true }, so that SLATE says its 1 € figure is an estimate. (2) It is wrong in scope. Only payments in euros count, and cash withdrawals are excluded; it isn't every card purchase. (3) 'Cancelable free from the next day' is out of date. It matches the 8 February 2008 press release ('dès le lendemain'), which appears to be where the wording came from. The current terms say changes made in the LCL Mes Comptes app take effect the next business day, and that round-ups accumulated before deactivation are not credited, a material loss the record leaves out. (4) It leaves out the insufficient-funds rule: a period's transfer that would overdraw the account or breach a regulated ceiling is cancelled in full. It also leaves out the eligible beneficiaries (Livret A, LDDS, Livret Jeune, non-regulated CSL; at most two, split 50/50; or a charity). (5) The timing is right: a fortnight ('quinzaine') for immediate-debit cards and month end for deferred-debit cards. (6) The record has no source of its own. The fr-lcl source string is the Compte à Terme Optilion page, which says nothing about System'Épargne. The source should be the card terms (e.g. the 2026 Visa Cléo Dispositions Générales) and https://www.lcl.fr/cartes-bancaires/system-epargne.

method: Unit choices: none. Every purchase is rounded up to the next whole pound (£1, fixed). There is no customer-chosen unit, no fixed amount per purchase, no multiplier and no remainder sweep. sourceAccount: The eligible Lloyds personal current account the debit card is linked to. On a joint account, the change from every holder's Lloyds debit card is saved.
destination: One chosen ('nominated') savings account. timing: Each purchase is rounded when the payment is taken from the account. The day's change is added up and moved as one transfer "at the start of the next working day". Friday's change arrives at the start of Monday. Saturday's, Sunday's and Monday's are added together at the end of Monday and arrive at the start of Tuesday. insufficientFunds: Before any transfer, Lloyds checks "the credit balance you've got available, less the amount of any card transactions you've made which haven't yet been taken from your account". The help page says "as long as you're in credit". The conditions don't say whether a part-transfer is made, or whether change that wasn't moved is dropped or carried to the next day.
refunds: Not reversed: "If your debit card transaction is cancelled or reversed (for example you get a refund), or if you tell us you think it was fraudulent, your change will stay in the savings account".
closure: Not stated. The conditions and help page say nothing about change that hasn't moved yet when the current or savings account closes.

optIn: Opt-in. In the ING App: open the Girokonto, tap 'Mehr' (3 dots), then 'Kleingeld Plus'. Online: Einstellungen > Produkteinstellungen Girokonto > Kleingeld Plus. The customer chooses the unit (1 or 5 euros) and the purpose (Sparen or, with Girokonto Future, Gutes tun). Rounding starts from the next bank working day (Monday to Friday). Changes take effect immediately, and the feature can be switched off at any time.
eligiblePurchases: All card payments made with the ING VISA Card [Debitkarte] or girocard [Debitkarte] linked to the selected Girokonto: in shops, online, and by mobile with Apple Pay or Google Pay, with PIN or contactless. The terms name only these two debit cards. No ING credit card is mentioned.
excluded: ATM cash withdrawals ('Bei Bargeldabhebungen am Automaten funktioniert Kleingeld Plus jedoch nicht'). Round amounts collect nothing (e.g. 20 or 25 euros; with the 5-euro unit, presumably any multiple of 5). Cards not linked to the selected Girokonto are excluded. Direct debits, transfers and standing orders are not card payments, so they are outside the feature by its definition. ING does not list them explicitly. Foreign-currency card payments are not addressed.
method: Round-up to the next unit, and the customer chooses the unit: the next full 1 euro or the next full 5 euros. ING gives no default. Examples: 2,30 rounds to 3,00 and saves 0,70 (at the 5-euro unit, 2,70 is saved); 2,73 rounds to 3,00; 12,89 rounds to 15,00. There is no fixed amount per purchase and no multiplier. In the Girokonto Future 'Gutes tun' mode there is an optional monthly maximum. ING does not say whether a cap exists in the savings mode.
sourceAccount: The ING Girokonto (or Girokonto Future) that the paying card is linked to.
destination: The customer's ING Extra-Konto: a Tagesgeld account, 'täglich ohne Kündigungsfrist fällig', which can pay out only to the reference Girokonto. In the Girokonto Future 'Gutes tun' mode the difference goes to the chosen share Förderprojekt instead, as a donation rather than savings.
timing: The rounding is computed on each card payment. 'Die gesammelten Beträge werden täglich von Ihrem Girokonto auf Ihr Extra-Konto überwiesen', so the day's amounts move in one daily transfer. Activation takes effect from the next bank working day, and changes take effect immediately.
insufficientFunds: The feature pauses while the Girokonto balance is under 20 euros, so that the account does not go into the red, and resumes once the balance is over 20 euros. The threshold is a floor on the current-account balance, not a check against the round-up amount. ING does not say whether round-ups from purchases made during a pause are dropped or carried over. 'Pausiert' suggests they are simply not collected, but this is not stated.
refunds: Not stated. No source says whether a round-up is reversed when a card purchase is refunded or cancelled. The FAQ notes only that pending card transactions ('Vorgemerkte Umsätze') can differ on partial cancellations, and that is unrelated to Kleingeld Plus.
closure: Not stated for the Girokonto or the Extra-Konto. The only rule found: switching off Girokonto Future ends Future and its Kleingeld Plus 'Gutes tun' mode 'spätestens am nächsten Werktag'. What happens to a day's not-yet-transferred round-ups on closure is unknown.

slateRecord: SLATE's ACCOUNT_LIFE['de-ing'].roundUp (sourced 2026-09-26) reads: 'Kleingeld Plus: every card payment is rounded up to the next full euro or next 5 euros (customer's choice); the rounding goes automatically to the Extra-Konto (Tagesgeld), available any time; can be changed or switched off at any time, starts the next bank working day.' The core is right and has not changed. It is incomplete in five ways: (1) It omits the 20-euro floor: the feature pauses while the Girokonto balance is under 20 euros. SLATE's nightly sweep (systems/accountlife.ts, registerAccountLife) instead moves the day's total only if current.balance >= pending, and otherwise drops it. That is a different rule. (2) 'Every card payment' should read: card payments with the ING VISA Card [Debitkarte] or girocard [Debitkarte] linked to that Girokonto, including Apple Pay and Google Pay, PIN or contactless, with ATM withdrawals excluded. (3) It omits that the collected amounts move daily. SLATE's nightly sweep happens to match. (4) Next bank working day applies to activation only; changes take effect immediately. (5) It omits the requirement to hold both a Girokonto and an Extra-Konto, and the Girokonto Future 'Gutes tun' alternative. The record's provenance is weak: the bank's source field is the Festgeld FAQ (https://www.ing.de/sparen-anlegen/sparen/festgeld/kundenservice/), not a Kleingeld Plus page. ROUND_UP_AMOUNT has no 'de-ing' entry, so SLATE always rounds to the next whole euro. That is exactly ING's 1-euro option, but the customer can pick 5 euros and ING states no default. Neither shape in ROUND_UP_AMOUNT fits: 'flat' is wrong, and the 'chosen' UI wording ('an amount you choose') describes an amount, not a choice between two units. A unit choice of 1 or 5 euros would match the bank; failing that, the record should say SLATE models the 1-euro option. SLATE's zero for round amounts (roundUpOf returns 0 when amount % 100 === 0) matches ING's 'Bei einem glatten Betrag ... wird nicht gesammelt' for the 1-euro unit. A related observation from the code, not a record error: SLATE accrues round-ups only on the debit-card food-purchase path (systems/spending.ts around lines 368-374), while ING rounds every card payment.

slateRecord: SLATE's roundUp reads: "KB스타뱅킹 '자투리 모으기' (added May 2020): on a scheduled day (daily/weekly/monthly) it withdraws the spare change below a chosen unit (1,000/5,000/10,000원) from the selected account and collects it." It is partly wrong and incomplete. (1) The cited source is the KB Star 정기예금 page (DP01000938), which says nothing about it; the words come from May 2020 news, and no official page read confirms the option today. (2) It omits that this is an open-banking 잔액 모으기 option that can pull from up to 5 accounts, including other banks', into a KB account that need not be savings. (3) The engine misapplies it. roundUpsOn() turns round-ups on for KB because the string exists, and with no ROUND_UP_AMOUNT entry roundUpFor() falls back to roundUpOf(), the change to the next whole unit per debit purchase. In KRW hundredths that is at most 0.99 won a purchase, and 0 on a whole-won price, against a bank sweep of up to 999, 4,999 or 9,999원 from the balance on a schedule. SLATE should either drop KB's roundUp until it is confirmed, or model a scheduled balance-remainder sweep with a customer-chosen unit.

excluded: Not purchase-based. The 저금통 itself cannot be used for card payments, bill payments or automatic debits, and accepts no deposits other than the automatic-saving rules.
method: Remainder sweep: the under-1,000원 part (1–999원) of the linked account's previous-day closing balance. (자동모으기, a separate rule: an AI-estimated amount each Saturday, base band 1,000–5,000원, optional raised band up to 10,000원. 캐시백 모으기: brand-coupon cashback.)

slateRecord: SLATE's roundUp reads: "저금통: linked to a KakaoBank 입출금 account; '동전 모으기' sweeps the under-1,000원 remainder (1-999원) of the account into the 저금통 on weekdays (Mon-Fri); '자동 모으기' saves an algorithm-chosen 1,000-10,000원 each Saturday; balance capped at 10만원; can be emptied to the linked account at any time." The words are mostly right but incomplete and slightly out of date. The source cited is /products/deposit, not /products/coinbox or the 2026-09-23 특약 and 상품설명서. The remainder is of the previous day's closing balance. Sweeps are skipped at a balance of 1,000원 or less (10,000원 or less for 자동모으기). 자동모으기 defaults to 1,000–5,000원 and goes up to 10,000원 only if the customer raises the band. 캐시백 모으기 is missing, and it can exceed the 10만원 cap. Eligibility since 2026-09-23 is 실명의 내국인 aged 14+, and 외국인통장 can be linked. Emptying is full withdrawal only. The serious error is in the engine. With no ROUND_UP_AMOUNT entry, roundUpFor() moves roundUpOf(debit purchase), the change to the next whole won (at most 99 hundredths, and 0 on whole-won prices), per purchase, into the person's savings. The bank instead sweeps up to 999원 each weekday from the balance whether or not anything was bought, into a separate 저금통 capped at 100,000원. SLATE should model a weekday remainder sweep, balance mod 1,000원, skipped at 1,000원 or less and capped at 100,000원, and stop treating it as a purchase round-up.

closure: The Cuenta Metas can be cancelled at any time and is closed within 24 hours. optIn: Open a Cuenta Modo Ahorro on the web or in the app, define a goal (name, amount, date), and select tools: card round-ups, a percentage of income, and/or periodic transfers. Then pick the rounding choice of €1, €2 or another amount.

eligibility: Debit: the account holder of a debit card's account. Only the account holder can set it up, and every debit card on that account is linked ('Eingöngu reikningseigandi getur stofnað þjónustuna. Öll debetkort sem tilheyra viðkomandi reikningi munu tengjast þjónustunni.'). Credit: holders of any Visa credit card ('handhöfum allra VISA-kreditkorta'), except a Plúskort (2020 page). No age limit is stated.
optIn: The customer registers in the online bank ('Sparað með kortanotkun', netbanki Card/CardSavings) and chooses the card, the savings account and the method. To stop, the 2019 terms say to contact the branch or contact centre, effective the same day. Whether it can now be stopped in the online bank or app is not stated.
eligiblePurchases: Only point-of-sale purchases of goods or services in shops or from service providers ('posafærslur'), domestic and foreign, on a debit card or a Visa credit card. Online (card-not-present) and contactless purchases are not addressed.
excluded: Anything that is not a purchase of goods or services. ATM withdrawals are excluded by implication, since the terms name only purchases, not withdrawals. Plúskort credit cards are excluded. A credit card transaction the merchant sends after the statement period has closed earns no saving. Saving is not made on overdraft. Transfers, bill payments and direct debits are not card purchases and are not covered.
method: The customer chooses one of two methods. (a) Round-up: each transaction is raised to the next 100, 500 or 1,000 kr and the difference is saved. The live 2026 text says only 'upp í næsta hundrað eða þúsund' and does not name 500. (b) Fixed amount: each transaction is raised by a fixed 100, 250, 500 or 1,000 kr. No default is stated. Bank examples: 1,250 kr rounded to the next 500 kr saves 250 kr; a 500 kr purchase raised by 250 kr saves 250 kr. Its illustration, at 20 transactions a month, averages 50 kr a purchase for next-100, 250 kr for next-500 and 500 kr for next-1,000. No multiplier and no remainder sweep. The saving is not on the merchant's receipt; the bank calculates it afterwards.
sourceAccount: Debit: the debit card's own account. Credit: not stated which account pays the saving, which is moved on the card account's due date.
destination: The savings account the customer chooses, entered by account number and the owner's kennitala. The terms allow three destinations: 'Leggja inn á eigin reikning hjá Landsbankanum', 'Leggja inn á reikning í eigu annars viðskiptavinar Landsbankans', or one of the charities in Landsbankinn's 'Góð málefni' service. Any Landsbankinn savings product the customer owns qualifies; none is singled out.
timing: Debit: at the end of each banking day the day's transactions are totalled and the saving moves the same day as one amount. Credit: computed at the end of each statement period and moved as one amount on the credit card account's due date (eindagi).
insufficientFunds: Debit: 'Ef ekki er innistæða á reikningi í lok bankadags er hætt við úttekt sparnaðar þess dags.' If the account has no funds at the end of the banking day, that day's whole saving is cancelled. By that wording it is dropped, not carried forward and not paid in part. The 2020 page adds 'ekki er sparað á yfirdrætti', so the overdraft is never used. Not stated: whether 'no funds' means less than the day's total or a balance at or below zero. Credit: no rule stated.
refunds: Not reversed. If a card transaction is cancelled, corrected or refunded to the card, the saving does not go back to the card and stays untouched in the savings account. This holds for debit and credit alike.
closure: The cardholder can close the service at any time, effective the same day. Landsbankinn may stop or cancel the service, in part or whole, without notice. Not stated: what happens to a day's or a statement period's uncollected saving when the service, the card account or the savings account closes.

sources.quote: We may allow you to ask us to transfer the difference between the amount of an Eligible Card Transaction and the nearest dollar amount from one eligible Account to another eligible ANZ Plus Account. We call this 'Round Ups'. You can ask us to do this in the ANZ Plus App. Sometimes transactions are made in foreign currencies. If an Eligible Card Transaction is made in a foreign currency, it'll be converted to Australian dollars, and we'll calculate the Round Up on that amount. We won't reverse or change a Round Up if an Eligible Card Transaction changes after you make it. You can ask us to stop Round Ups in the ANZ Plus App. Either Joint Account holder can ask us to Round Up Eligible Card Transactions for an eligible Joint Account. We may disable or suspend Round Ups, and we may not notify you if we do this. [Definitions:] Eligible Card Transaction means a transaction we classify as a Visa Debit Card or Digital Wallet transaction based on information available to us. eligibility: ANZ Plus customers only. optIn: In the ANZ Plus app: 'Go to the Card icon. Swipe to the find the card you'd like to Round Up transactions from. Look for Round Ups and select Enable. Toggle on Round Ups and choose the amount and eligible account you'd like to Round Up to.' The unit and the destination can be changed later, and Round Ups can be stopped in the app at any time.
eligiblePurchases: 'a transaction we classify as an ANZ Plus Visa Debit card or digital wallet transaction' (contactless and online Visa Debit purchases fall within that; neither is named separately). Purchases in a foreign currency are converted to AUD first, then rounded.
excluded: 'direct debits, BPAY, Pay Anyone payments and ATM withdrawals' (the terms say these are 'generally' excluded). Credit cards are not mentioned; the definition covers only Visa Debit and digital wallet transactions.
method: Unit choices: the next multiple of $1, $2, $5 or $10, chosen by the customer. The 2023 launch release gave $2 as the default; the current pages state no default. The amount moved is the difference between the purchase and the next multiple of the chosen unit. A purchase already at a multiple moves nothing. Worked examples for a $13 purchase: $1 unit moves $0, $2 moves $1, $5 moves $2, $10 moves $7. There is no fixed amount per purchase, no multiplier and no cap stated.
sourceAccount: The ANZ Plus account the card is linked to, which is ANZ Plus Everyday ('from one eligible Account').
destination: An 'eligible ANZ Plus account': an ANZ Plus savings account (the Growth Saver's Savings Jar, or a goal within it) or an ANZ Plus Home Loan. Round Ups between joint accounts held with different people are not allowed.
timing: Each purchase separately, on the day it is made: 'the Round Up will appear on the day you make the transaction and the transaction will appear on the day it is processed'. There is no daily batch.
insufficientFunds: Not stated by ANZ. The general terms say only that a transaction with insufficient funds 'may overdraw your Account or we may decline or not process a transaction', which is not specific to Round Ups.
refunds: Not reversed: 'We won't reverse or change a Round Up if an Eligible Card Transaction changes after you make it.' A reversed pre-authorisation also leaves its Round Up in place.
closure: Not stated in the current terms or support pages. Search-engine snippets of an older version of 'How do I end a savings goal?' said ANZ would try to redirect Round Ups from an ended goal to the Savings Jar, but the current page (2025-06-26) no longer says so.

sources.quote: Save the Change rounds up all your eligible transactions throughout the day, then at the end of the day, adds up each of the individual rounded amounts and makes one transfer to the nominated savings account(s) overnight.

You can choose to round: 1. EFTPOS transactions (including Visa Debit if you have one) or 2. EFTPOS + other electronic transactions including: EFTPOS, Visa Debit, Bill Payments, Automatic Payments, Direct Debits, One-Off Payment, FastPhone Bill Payments, Contactless Payments (Apple Pay and Google Pay). You can also set your transactions to be rounded to the nearest multiple of $1, $2, $5 or $10.

Save the Change doesn't apply on transactions involving: Credit Cards (including refunded purchases). Cheques. Transfers. Transactions processed in an ASB branch or by our Contact Centre. All account and service fees (including other bank ATM charges). Any interest charges and any credit paid into accounts. All overseas transactions.

You'll simply need both an eligible ASB transaction and savings account. ... You can Save the Change on the following ASB transaction accounts: Streamline, Omni, Unlimited, Graduate, Tertiary, Job starter's, Headstart, Orbit, Orbit FastTrack ... You can Save the Change to the following accounts: FastSaver, Savings On Call, PrizeSaver, Headstart, ASB Cash Fund, Moneymaker, Accelerater, Flexisave.

the total rounded amount is split evenly amongst the number of savings accounts you nominate. If the amount can't be evenly split between all accounts, the first savings account listed will receive any additional amounts. ... You can choose up to 10 ASB savings accounts to receive your savings. They can be your own ASB savings accounts, someone else's ASB savings accounts or a combination of both.
If you have an arranged overdraft limit, then your Save the Change transfer will happen as usual if it keeps you within that limit.

If you close your accounts Save the Change will switch off. If you have nominated more than one savings account, Save the Change will switch Saving the Change to the remaining account(s), and switch off when the last nominated savings account is closed. If you change your transaction or savings account, Save the Change can go with you.

If for any reason we can't transfer your savings into one of your nominated savings accounts, the funds will simply be returned to your transaction account. ... If you only have one nominated savings account, we'll stop Save the Change until you choose a new savings account.
Achieve your savings goal sooner with Save the Change. You can round up electronic purchases you make to the nearest dollar and the change goes into another account.

eligibility: An eligible ASB transaction account together with an ASB savings account. Eligible personal transaction accounts (list last updated 25 Sep 2023): Streamline, Omni, Unlimited, Graduate, Tertiary, Job starter's, Headstart, Orbit and Orbit FastTrack. Some business and rural accounts also qualify. A joint transaction account qualifies only if either holder can authorise transactions alone; any joint savings account can receive.
optIn: In the ASB Mobile app, select the transaction account, then More options > Save the Change setup. In FastNet Classic, Menu > Financial wellbeing > Save the Change > Set up. The customer chooses the transaction account, the payment type (option 1 or 2), the rounding amount and the savings account(s), then accepts the Save the Change terms. Those terms are shown only during setup and are not public: ASB's published Personal Banking terms (Oct 2025), FastNet Classic terms (Jul 2022) and Mobile Banking terms (Nov 2021) do not mention Save the Change. It can be switched off at any time in the app or FastNet Classic.
eligiblePurchases: The customer chooses one of two options. Option 1 covers EFTPOS transactions, including Visa Debit. Option 2 covers EFTPOS plus other electronic payments: Visa Debit, bill payments, automatic payments, direct debits, one-off payments, FastPhone bill payments and contactless (Apple Pay, Google Pay).
excluded: Credit cards (including refunded purchases), cheques, transfers, transactions processed in a branch or by the Contact Centre, all account and service fees (including other banks' ATM charges), interest charges, any credit paid into accounts, and all overseas transactions. ASB does not say whether ATM cash withdrawals are excluded.
method: Unit choices: the next multiple of $1, $2, $5 or $10, chosen by the customer and changeable at any time. No default is stated on the current pages; a 2021 ASB media release says Save the Change 'starts by rounding purchases to the nearest dollar'. The amount is the difference between each eligible transaction and the next multiple ($32.50 at $2 moves $1.50). There is no fixed amount per purchase and no multiplier.
sourceAccount: The nominated ASB everyday transaction account.
destination: One to ten ASB savings accounts, the customer's own or someone else's. The day's total is split evenly, and the first account listed gets any odd cents. Listed eligible savings accounts (2023): FastSaver, Savings On Call, PrizeSaver, Headstart, ASB Cash Fund, Moneymaker, Accelerater and Flexisave. Savings Plus Monthly is not on that list, but its product page promotes Save the Change. With Donate the Change, part goes to an ASB charity partner (Youthline, Hato Hone St John or KidsCan), split evenly with savings at the end of each day.
timing: Each eligible transaction is rounded during the day. At the end of the day the individual round-ups are added up and moved in one overnight transfer.
insufficientFunds: With an arranged overdraft, the transfer goes ahead as long as it keeps the account within the limit, and 'the rounded-up value will increase your overdrawn balance'. Without an overdraft, only the 2010 launch news says the transfer happens 'only ... if there were sufficient funds ... at the end of the day'. ASB's own pages do not say whether a short day's change is dropped, carried forward or partly transferred.
refunds: Not stated. Credits paid into the account are not themselves rounded. ASB does not say whether the round-up on a later-refunded purchase is reversed.
closure: Closing the accounts switches Save the Change off. If several savings accounts were nominated, it moves to the remaining ones and switches off when the last closes. If a transfer into a savings account fails, 'the funds will simply be returned to your transaction account'. A product change, such as Headstart to Streamline, carries the setup across.
